finding:
Partial landing. §1.1.3 p. 12 asserts, without proof, that the singleton-base Hardy–Sobolev space agrees with W^{s,2}(G). The preceding p. 11 definition assumes a<b and fixes Haar. Chapter 9 does define the singleton: (9.2.2.31) takes the supremum over a≤b and closed subintervals of I and completes S_E(G), with canonical Haar and real s≥0. At I={0} only [0,0] contributes, and the maximum in (9.2.2.34) equals 1. Definition 9.1.2.1 denotes W^{s,2}(G) by H_w^s on the dual with Plancherel measure in (9.1.2.2); the Fourier realization of that dual Sobolev norm runs on the double dual, identified with G, with the original Haar by dual Plancherel normalization. This is the physical-variable weighted L² norm (9.1.2.3). The reading uses the weighted realization in Lemma 9.1.1.2; the printed juxtaposition of C_c on the dual with the Fourier transform in (9.1.1.3) is not a definition of a finite weighted Fourier norm on every compactly supported continuous input (see the handoff). That physical-variable norm agrees on test functions with the singleton norm for the same Haar; replacing μ by cμ changes the identity norm by sqrt(c), not the test functions or completeness. Equality of the test-function norms alone does not give density.

For the actual identity-module G=R_{>0}, canonical dt/t, and x=log t, the new Lean module identifies the exact density with (1+|x|²)^(s/2) and proves that arbitrary elements of the full weighted L², not only of a second profile image, are norm approximable by compactly supported profiles in the original Masullo.logWeightedProfiles univ via Masullo.logSobolevAllToLp. On the log line local finiteness gives regularity and compactly supported continuous approximants in this same measure. Mollification on the log line gives smooth approximants with support in a fixed compact neighborhood and uniform error controlled in the same weighted L². Smooth compact support gives a Schwartz factor after multiplication by exp(a*x) for each real a; the accepted embedding gives the a.e. class of that profile. The accepted norm, faithfulness and dt/t change of variables are in Proofs/Theorems/RadialHardySobolevCompletion.lean at 198b80a26562ac7e97db2c38a75ddb6200e388fe, using Masullo.map_volume_exp_eq_restrict_realMultiplicative. Thus the full log-coordinate weighted L² is a concrete complete realization in the radial case, for all real s (an extension of the printed s≥0). No general compact-kernel density or arbitrary-to-canonical Haar comparison is formalized here, nor a Lean Fourier realization on the abstract dual or an equivalence of abstract Completion types. See .godel/formalize/radial-singleton-sobolev.md for the exact source reading and ordinary-import replay.
retry: For a general second-countable surjectively modulated G, first check a continuous homomorphic split and its Haar pushforward; the accepted Masullo.logVolume_prod_of_split_haar is conditional on a supplied split. Under G≃R×K with K the compact module-one kernel, verify that radial smooth compactly supported functions times continuous characters χ of K descend to smooth compactly supported tests on G/ker χ (K/ker χ is a closed subgroup of the circle and hence an elementary compact Lie group). Check the admissible compact-kernel Schwartz–Bruhat stage and every exponential weight there. Prove density of the span by compact-character density and weighted radial L² density in the split product measure, and finiteness of the singleton norm on general all-weight stages from their Schwartz decay in the radial variable. Separately determine the Haar scalar via module windows (canonical means compact factor of mass one) and match the physical variable realization by the same Haar or the explicit scalar rescaling; do not use a merely equivalent Hilbert topology as an identity isometry.
